#5513 

Earlier , we were not visiting arguments of Elemental Function . This PR tries to incorporate this thing in array_op.

MRE 1
```
program test 
  integer :: A(3) = [1,2,3]
  logical :: X(3)
  integer :: tol = 2
  X = abs(A) <= max(tol, tol * maxval(abs(A)))
  print *, X
end program
```

Output 
```
(lf) ansh_mehta@DESKTOP-VJGRLON:/mnt/d/lfortran2/lfortran$ ./src/bin/lfortran try.f90
T    T    T
```

MRE 2
```
program test 
  integer :: A(3) = [1,2,3]
  logical :: X(3)
  integer :: tol = 2
  X = abs(A) <= max(tol,maxval(abs(A)))
  print *, X
end program
```

Output 
```
(lf) lordansh@LordAnsh:~/dev/lfort2/lfortran$ ./src/bin/lfortran try.f90
T    T    T
```

MRE 3
```
program test 
integer :: A(3,2) = reshape([1,2,3,4,5,6], [3,2])
integer :: X(2)
X = abs(sum(A, dim=1))
print *, X
end program
```

Output 
```
(lf) lordansh@LordAnsh:~/dev/lfort2/lfortran$ ./src/bin/lfortran try.f90
6    15

with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 implicit real(i), integer(b)

with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352

with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 with F77 validation suite FCVS_95 (see #480 ) demonstrated that our support for `IMPLICIT` statements was incomplete, particularly in that we only allow one _implicit-spec_ per _implicit-stmt_, instead of an _implicit-spec-list_.  An example statement that is now properly accepted is:
```f90
implicit real(i), integer(b)
```

 This PR adds that support, with changes in the AST grammar, the parser, AST symbol table visitor, and AST->src conversion.  AST->ASR conversion already supported this structure.

The PR also updates the test reference AST files, and adds the new test `implicit13`.  After these changes, FCVS_95 tests that use _implicit-spec-list_ no longer fail (on those statements, at least).

This closes #5352 
This closes #3113 Description

Fixes https://github.com/lfortran/lfortran/issues/5294

The program linked in the issue (or the one added as a test case in this PR) already works without any use of `--implicit-interface` (and it's expected to work), but this PR focuses on making that program work with use of `--implicit-interface` as well, as *POT3D* needs `--implicit-interface` flag necessarily.

## Changes in ASR

Currently the MRE in the linked issue when run with `--implicit-interface` on the current-main raises the below error:
```console
ASR verify pass error: ASR verify: The symbol table was not found in the scope of `symtab`.
 --> /Users/gxyd/OpenSource/lfortran/test.f90:3:16
  |
3 |     integer :: g = 2
  |                ^^^^^ failed here

ASR verify pass error: Var::m_v `g` cannot point outside of its symbol table
 --> /Users/gxyd/OpenSource/lfortran/test.f90:9:16
  |
9 |     call sub2 (g)
  |                ^ failed here

```

Fixes https://github.com/lfortran/lfortran/issues/5294

The program linked in the issue (or the one added as a test case in this PR) already works without any use of `--implicit-interface` (and it's expected to work), but this PR focuses on making that program work with use of `--implicit-interface` as well, as *POT3D* needs `--implicit-interface` flag necessarily.

 --> /Users/gxyd/OpenSource/lfortran/test.f90:9:16
  |
9 |     call sub2 (g)
  |                ^ failed here

```fortran

real, dimension(2) :: drratior=0.0 ---------> real, dimension(2) :: drratior

.entry:
  call void @_lpython_call_initial_functions(i32 %0, i8** %1)

  br label %return

}

```fortran
module main_module

contains

   subroutine sub(int)
      integer,intent(in) :: int
      print *, int
      if (int /= 6) error stop
   end subroutine sub

end module main_module


program main

   use main_module

   procedure(sub), pointer :: p_sub
   p_sub => sub
   call p_sub(6)

end program main
```

am using this to write down and iterate on design: Brief: struct `LocationManager` contains all information we need, and in case of multiple files we wish to serialise `LocationManager` which contains `strings`, `boolean` and `vectors` of `uint32_t` which can be serialised and loaded during deserialisation. After deserialisation we need to fetch existing `LocationManager` struct and merge new one with this. To merge we need to set `offset` which is nothing but `pos + 1` of last file. Detailed: - Pass `LCompilers::LocationManager lm` to `save_mod_files` and pass it to `save_asr` where before writing `Full ASR:` write entire `LocationManager`. - By step 1, we have location manager in a serialized format, next is to deserialize it - Pass `lm` to `ast_to_asr` and with every `ASRUtils::load_module`, we invoke `find_and_load_module` and eventually `load_modfile`, in `load_serialised_asr`, deserialize `lm` struct and merge it with existing `LocationManager` passed as arguments. We need not to worry about duplication, as `load_module` only loads module once. With this we will have the two structs merged. Now the next question is for `call sub()` the `pos` will be corresponding to file `a.f90`, and thereby `index = bisection(file_ends, pos)` gives us index corresponding to `a.f90` and not module file. Even if we have information, we are not able to identify if `sub()` belongs to which `index`. ```fortran subroutine add() end subroutine program expr2 use module_expr2 implicit none integer :: x x = (2+3)*5 print *, x, xy call sub() call add() end program ``` cc @certik ","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/lfortran/lfortran/issues/comments/2558993008/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"performed_via_github_app":null}}
